title: The field-capture decision record's payload, read shape, message id set, panel id, parameter names and login name have no source
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1 to A2.5, A2.8 and A2.14 field catalog; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry, T3.2 LOV-DECISION, T-A.1 API-P7-006 and API-P7-007, T-A.2; legacy RWB-E2-024 sections 4, 11, 12 and 14
description: Six values of this story are not fixed by any source: (1) the payload field set of a field-capture decision entry - no column of TSD P7 v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry holds the document reference, the client file ID, the document type code, the capture kind, the capture time or the message id of a refusal, and no source says whether they are new columns or jsonb members of recommendation or actions; (2) the request and answer shape of the two reads - T-A.2 API-P7-006 fixes the query as caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page and size, with no object-reference filter, and the T-A.2 answer names DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry without their field set; (3) the message id set - MSG-P7-009 is named by the FSD P7 v3 exception flows and its text is never written out, no source writes the text of MSG-GEN-006, and no message id exists for an entry refused for a missing object reference or for a document with no entry; (4) the panel or screen id that would show the DOCATT entries of a case beside the documents, since SCR-30 and SCR-31 are rwb-document's and the decision screen SCR-11 is named only by another story; (5) the parameter names and version labels of the ledger ingest target of 5 minutes and the daily chain-check time of 02:00, which Architecture v5 slide 28 and JOB-14 name as values but no source names as parameter rows; (6) the name of the per-service database login of DP-02.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 lists DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and DF-DEC-028 to DF-DEC-031 with no document, client file, capture, type or message column; TSD P7 v2 T3.2 LOV-DECISION is not enumerated at all and LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS holds WAITING, HELD_NO_LIMIT, APPROVED, REFUSED and RETURNED; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-006 request is 'Query: caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page, size'; FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 refuse with MSG-P7-009 naming ruleVersion and decisionCode, whose text no source writes; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-P7-001-02 gives the seven field groups of an entry (inputsRef, ruleId and ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId and approvalLevel, finalCall, actions and outcome, decidedAt, prevHash, entryHash) and none of the capture facts; legacy RWB-E2-024 section 11 names DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 only
area: P7 decision record: entry payload, read contract, messages, panel, parameters, service login
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the data steward, the P5 business analyst and the business owner
proposed: At design time of wave 2 the solution architect, the data steward, the P5 business analyst and the business owner agree and approve, as reference data and as the OpenAPI of the service: the capture columns of decision_log_entry (new columns or jsonb members), the object-reference filter of the read and the answer field set, the message ids and their texts, the panel id of the decision-log view, the parameter names and version labels of the ingest target and the chain check, and the per-service login name; until then the story holds the assumed shape of ASM-B-P7-03-E2024-1, ASM-B-P7-03-E2024-2 and ASM-B-P7-03-E2024-3 and its seven criteria stand on that shape

title: The decision code of a field-capture entry is D6.5 in the legacy metadata but DOCATT on the store path
source: Legacy RWB-E2-024 metadata row Decision D6.5, section 4 step 6 and section 11 DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018; Recovery Workbench Case and Workflow Model v5 (D6.5 and D6.6 Guarantee claim) and Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-GUA-01 to R-GUA-19; FSD P5 Document hub v3 AC-ALT-P5-010-01 and AC-P5-012-01; Decision Log v9 D-RCV-31; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003 and T3.2 LOV-DECISION; FSD P7 v3 A2.14 field catalog
description: The legacy story tags the field capture with Decision D6.5, while the case and workflow model and the routing logic give D6.5 and D6.6 to the Thai Credit Guarantee claim stage (R-GUA-01 to R-GUA-19, decision 'Guarantee claim, D6.5 and D6.6') and the Deed in Lieu inspection the legacy rationale names is a treatment stage, not a D6 sub-decision. The entry the store writes is called DOCATT in every document path of the key (legacy section 4 step 6, FSD P5 v3, D-RCV-31) and TSD P7 v2 DF-DEC-003 types decision_code as varchar(8) against a list whose content is not enumerated. A story cannot carry both codes on one entry, and FSD P7 v3 A2.14 describes the code domain as D5.1 to D9.3, X1 to X7 or an access event, none of which is DOCATT.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-024 metadata 'Decision | D6.5' and section 2 naming the deed in lieu inspection step WITH_FIELD_INSPECTION (R-DIL-22) and the repossessed vehicle photo record (CTL-38); Case and Workflow Model v5 row 'Guarantee claim, D6.5 and D6.6'; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-GUA-01 to R-GUA-19 in the D6.5, D6.6 route set; FSD P5 v3 AC-ALT-P5-010-01 'one DOCATT decision log entry is written by the store'; Decision Log v9 D-RCV-31 'writes a DOCATT audit entry'; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 decision_code varchar(8) LOV-DECISION
area: Decision code reference data and ledger content, P7 rwb-decision with P5 rwb-document
owner_role: Business analyst, P7, with the business analyst of P5 rwb-document and the data steward
proposed: Approve DOCATT as the value of LOV-DECISION carried on every document-attach entry, keep D6.5 as the routing-decision tag of the legacy story and not as the code of the entry, and record the decision in the reference-data register of rwb-case; the legacy Decision field is then read as the route that produced the capture, not as the ledger code

title: No source settles whether an item the store refuses leaves a DOCATT entry
source: Legacy RWB-E2-024 section 4 step 6, section 11 and exception X12; RWB-ITG-E2024-ITG sections 12.2, 12.8 and AC1; FSD P7 v3 A2.2 AC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-02; TSD P7 v2 T3.1
description: The legacy story writes the DOCATT entry for every document the store stores (section 4 step 6: 'the store writes the document, the DOCATT decision log entry and DocumentStored') and says nothing about an item the store refuses, while its principle 5 test TC-E2-024-17 refuses the item when the log write fails. The integration story of the key reads the decision log 'for the DOCATT entry of each stored document and for each refused item' in its flow and twelve-step harness, and then describes the same assertion as 'the absent entry per refused item' in sections 12.2 and 12.8. The P7 slice of this key requires one record per stored document and one per item refused, so the two readings cannot both stand.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-024 section 4 step 6 and exception X12 'The decision log write fails for an item | Item refused; nothing stored for it | MSG-P7-003'; RWB-ITG-E2024-ITG flow step 9 'records whether the DOCATT entry exists for each stored document and for each item the store refused', AC1 'ten DOCATT decision records are on rwb.decision-record.v1', and sections 12.2 and 12.8 'the absent entry per refused item'; FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 AC-EXC-P7-002-02 'a failed write stops the action'
area: Decision record scope, P7 rwb-decision with the wave 2 integration harness
owner_role: Business analyst, P7, with the P5 business analyst and the integration lead of RWB-ITG-E2024-ITG
proposed: Approve one entry per stored document and one per item the store refuses, with the final call carrying the item result (ACCEPTED, REFUSED or QUARANTINED) and the message id of a refusal, and correct RWB-ITG-E2024-ITG sections 12.2 and 12.8 to assert the entry of a refused item rather than its absence; a DUPLICATE item is neither and resolves to the entry of the item received first

title: The extraction decision record's payload, value sets, read shape and screen id have no source
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1 to A2.4 and A2.8; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry, T3.2 LOV-DECISION and LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, T-A.1 API-P7-006 and API-P7-007, T-A.2

title: Where the generation record is written, and whether its failure stops the generation, is read two ways
source: Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service writes its own decision_record and publishes DecisionRecorded), slide 28 (recorded locally at once, then sealed centrally within 5 minutes, strict mode only at points of no return), slide 41 (P7 owns the central decision ledger); FSD P7 v3 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P7-002-02 (a failed write stops the action); legacy RWB-E2-026 AC7 and BR7 (the decision log write fails and the generation does not proceed); the work package slice (the record is written in rwb_decision in the same transaction as the generation it records)
section: Sections 1, 4, 5, 7 (AC4, AC9), 8 (BR13) and 13 of the story
description: The sources disagree on two points and this slice has to pick one. Point one: Architecture v5 slide 20 and slide 28 make the record local to each of the 19 services and collect it into the rwb-decision ledger within 5 minutes, while the work package slice and legacy RWB-E2-026 AC7 read the record as written in the ledger and the generation as stopping when that write fails. Point two: FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-02 makes a failed write stop the action it records, which a producer-side write can enforce inside one transaction but an asynchronous ledger append cannot. A generation set is not one of the four strict-mode points of no return of slide 28 (debt transfer, write-off, auction sale, title transfer), so the 5-minute catch-up applies to it as it does to every other decision, and yet the legacy criterion keeps the generation blocked. The slice resolves this by keeping the producer write inside the generation transaction and the ledger append atomic and idempotent, and by refusing the generation only when the record write itself cannot be made.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20 'DB Own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record' and 'EVT DecisionRecorded to rwb.decision-record.v1 (ledger in rwb-decision)'; slide 28 'rwb-decision reads rwb.decision-record.v1 into the ledger within 5 minutes' and 'Strict mode for points of no return: Debt transfer, write-off, auction sale and title transfer'; slide 41 'P7 rwb-decision: approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry'; FSD P7 v3 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P7-002-02 'the write raises DecisionLogUnavailableException And the case owner stays empty'; legacy RWB-E2-026 X5 and AC7 'the response is 503 with MSG-P7-003; no document row exists and the draft file is removed'
area: Architecture: decision record write path and transaction boundary
owner_role: Solution architect, with the platform team and the P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: Adopt the producer-side write inside the generation transaction with the atomic, idempotent ledger append of this story and keep MSG-P7-003 as the refusal of the record write path, so legacy AC7 holds word for word; confirm at the architecture review whether a generation set belongs in strict mode, and if it does, add the ledger acknowledgement to the generation flow as its own change

title: PAYMENT_MATCH registry governance: shapes, decision-record payload, message set and promotion and rollback semantics are not specified
source: RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2.md sections 3, 7, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 16; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.7 (AC-P7-007-01, AC-ALT-P7-007-01 and -02, AC-EXC-P7-007-01 to -05); TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1, T-A.1 and T-A.2
description: The sources give the load and version-list shapes, the six checks and the four-eyes rule, but not the whole governance interface. Missing: the rollback request body and answer beyond a reason and the two versions; the dry-run body beyond testResult (total, passed, failed, failedScenarioIds) and dryRunCounts; the decision code of a governance record, and whether load, approve, promote and rollback share one code or take four (the only code the sources name for this key is D5, which is the match entry rwb-payment writes); the rule_id and rule_version values a governance record carries; the text of MSG-P3-015; a further PAYMENT_MATCH version label for a refused load below the test-case minimum; the promote operation, which has no path because the promotion is the JOB-20 Schedule; the rule_test_case record fields beyond the test case and the expected and actual result; the behaviour of the load, approve and rollback operations with the rwb.p3.drools switch off; and the answer of the version list when no version is in force on a business date.
evidence: Legacy section 12 gives POST and GET /admin/rule-packages/PAYMENT_MATCH/versions with their fields and errors but no rollback body; section 14 names no message for a successful promotion or rollback and no text for MSG-P3-015; FSD P7 A2.7 AC-P7-007-01 states the change log content but no payload, and AC-EXC-P7-007-05 names MSG-P3-015 without its text; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 declares decision_log_entry and approval only, with no rule table and no governance decision code.

title: PAYMENT_MATCH version label and valid-from date conflict between RWB-E2-027 and RWB-E2-042
source: RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2.md sections 3 and 7 (PM-2026.12 in force from 2026-12-01); RWB P3 E2042 APP Epic 2 rule packages in Drools v1.md section 3 and AC2 (PMT-2026.12, valid from 2026-12-15, 3 rows, 58 scenarios); Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 16 (labels look like ALLOC-2026.12)
description: The same package, with the same three rows EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL and the same 58 scenarios, carries two version labels and two valid-from dates: the RWB-E2-027 story has PM-2026.12 from 2026-12-01 and the RWB-E2-042 slice has PMT-2026.12 from 2026-12-15. One registry row cannot carry both, and a promotion of both would put two versions of one row set in force on two dates.
evidence: Legacy section 3 names PAYMENT_MATCH version PM-2026.12 in force from 2026-12-01 and legacy section 7 builds its Background on it; RWB-P3-E2042-APP AC2 names PMT-2026.12 from 2026-12-15 with 3 rows and 58 scenarios; the Temporal and Drools design gives the label shape as package prefix plus year and month.
owner_role: Rule owner RW-COE, with the P7 and P3 solution architects
proposed: One row per package version: keep PM-2026.12 from 2026-12-01 as the RWB-E2-027 value under the fill order of R7.3, record PMT-2026.12 and 2026-12-15 as the E2-042 value, and reconcile the two into one label and one valid-from date before the PAYMENT_MATCH package is promoted in SIT.

title: The rule-package operations: the legacy P4 attribution and the /admin/rule-versions paths against P7 and /admin/rule-package-versions
source: RWB E2 027 Payment matching rules with the data team v2.md section 12 (the load named P4 under /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-packages/PAYMENT_MATCH/versions); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api rows GET and POST /admin/rule-packages, GET /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run, POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve and .../rollback, and GET and POST /admin/rule-versions with POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve and .../rollback (all owner P7, asm ASM-A6-api-3); Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41

owner_role: P7 solution architect, with the API specification owner

title: No source gives the value set or the wire shape this story needs: the append request and answer, the ledger read and its page, the reason codes, the run read field set, the text of MSG-P7-009 and the DP-02 login name
source: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 8, 10, 12, 13 and 14 against TSD P7 v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1, FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 and A2.14.3.2, and Architecture v5 slide 20
description: The legacy story fixes the facts of the record and none of the shapes. It names the decision code D6 and itself calls it an assumed code, and neither TSD P7 v2 T3.2 nor any LOV table the extract carries lists the values of LOV-DECISION, so the code and the verdict list ACCEPTED, CORRECTED and REJECTED are carried as reference data whose values are read and not written. It gives no code set for the reason of a correction or a rejection. It gives the decision log mapping field by field but no request or answer body: the append has no path and no method in the service, because TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 documents only the two reads API-P7-006 and API-P7-007, and the field set of the DecisionLogPage and of the DecisionLogEntry the reads return is not written out. The run read of rwb-agent and the authorise call of rwb-access are consumed without a documented request or answer. The text of MSG-P7-009 is named by FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 and written out nowhere. The name of the per-service database login of DP-02 is not given. The item key of the summary, the idempotency key form and the reason length limit are the only shapes the legacy gives (item key SUMMARY, a reason of at most 1,000 characters).
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 8 BR3 ('decision D6 (LOV-DECISION, assumed code)'), BR4 and BR5; section 10 (roles RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, SY-AGENT, SY-DECLOG, RW-COE); section 12 (the decision log mapping and AgentFeedbackRequest with the reason of at most 1,000 characters); section 13 (migration V10_008 and the panel labels); section 14 (MSG-P7-005, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031), T3.2 (LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-PRODUCT and no LOV-DECISION) and T-A.1 (API-P7-006, API-P7-007); FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 AC-EXC-P7-002-05 (MSG-P7-009 naming decisionCode), A2.14.3.2 and A2.14.4.1; Architecture v5 slide 20 (every service writes its own decision records), slide 14 (rwb-decision schema rwb_decision) and slide 41 (schema and login per service)
proposed: Agree the three operation shapes, the two list value sets and the two message texts at the wave 2 contract review of RWB-P10-E2028-CON and of this service: the append on POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log with the request and the DecisionRecord answer of section 12.1, the two reads with the DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry field sets of TSD P7 v2 T3.1, LOV-DECISION with the value D6 and a verdict list with the three values, a reason-code list, the text of MSG-P7-009 and the name of the rwb-decision login. Until then the story builds and tests against the values of ASM-B-P7-03-E2028-1 to ASM-B-P7-03-E2028-4 and the contract fakes of section 12.8.

title: The metadata rows name no build dependency and the agent contract only, while the DP table of the story adds six platform contracts and one rwb-case contract and the story consumes two further operations
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP table rows DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19 against the plan story record of RWB-P7-E2028-APP and the Ownership Map
description: The story record carries Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P10-E2028-CON. The seven patterns the story applies add seven contracts the metadata does not carry: DP-03 H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-07 H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-09 H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, DP-10 H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-15 H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and DP-19 H RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Two operations the story consumes are named by no pattern and by no metadata row: the P3 case read the scope filter is applied to and the P4 authorise call of the Decision log right, because DP-08 is not among the patterns of the key. Each of the seven is a platform contract of waves 0 and 1 or a published contract of another service, so none blocks the build beyond Day 1, but a worker cannot choose between the plan line and the pattern table without a ruling, and the two consumed operations would otherwise be built against a contract that no row tracks.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19 and R5.7 rules 1 to 3; the story record of RWB-P7-E2028-APP (H [], C ['RWB-P10-E2028-CON']); Ownership Map api row GET /cases/{caseId} (P3) and table agent_run (P10); Architecture v5 slide 14 (P4 IN: POST /authorise) and slide 41 (P4 first API path /authorise); sections 3, 12.2 and 13 of this story
proposed: Read the H list of the story as None plus the six platform contracts the DP table names, and the C list as RWB-P10-E2028-CON plus C RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the published contracts of the P3 case read and the P4 authorise call; the platform contracts are delivery prerequisites of the service template and not per-story blockers, and the story stays Day 1.
